public_rationale: At its October 13, 2026 briefing, the IMF described strong market risk appetite and an AI-related correction as a risk [e1]. Reuters reporting published October 27, 2026 described a 40% fall in China's STAR50 index in less than four months and an approximately 20% fall in its broad blue-chip index from June highs [e2]. The report documents regional losses and identifies several possible contributors; it does not establish a collapse of the broader AI boom centered on major US technology companies [e2]. The evidence does not establish both a qualifying collapse and market losses attributable to it, leaving the forecast unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: The Chinese selloff alone does not establish the broader collapse required by the contract [e2].
The report does not isolate losses caused by an AI-boom collapse from other contributors to the selloff [e2].
The Chinese market figures come from news reporting rather than direct exchange or index-provider records [e2].
The IMF briefing describes conditions on October 13, 2026 and does not establish subsequent market conditions [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: When the AI bubble pops, there will be measurable damage to the stock market.

statement.excerpt: There will be measurable damage to the stock market, but more importantly tens of thousands of people will lose their jobs and a depression will begin in the tech industry.

from_speaker: There will be measurable damage to the stock market
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion makes this conditional on the AI bubble popping.
The plain reading is an observable stock-market loss attributable to a collapse of the AI investment boom discussed in the post.
The context points to the broader boom centered on major US technology companies. A regional collapse is relevant but does not automatically establish that antecedent.
Major US indexes and representative technology or AI stock baskets are reasonable measures. No minimum percentage loss is imposed.
No deadline or fixed period after the collapse is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Independent evidence establishes the relevant AI-boom collapse, and market data with credible event analysis show an attributable loss in stock-market value.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The relevant collapse occurs and sufficiently complete market evidence establishes that it produced no measurable stock-market loss. Continued investment or the absence of a collapse cannot contradict the forecast.

evidence.explanation: The IMF described continuing market optimism and discussed an AI correction as a risk. This does not establish the forecast's collapse condition or rule out subsequent developments.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Independent documentation of a qualifying collapse of the broader AI boom, dated index or representative stock-basket returns, and credible analysis separating its effects from other shocks. A measurable market loss attributable to the collapse would support the claim. Sufficiently complete evidence that the collapse produced no measurable stock-market loss would contradict it.
